classification.difficultyReason: Interpret each theory as an increase or decrease multiplier, divide the present volume to recover the original, and round to tens.

content.prompt: A research institute is trying to find out how much water Lake William had in it 8000 years ago. The lake now contains 7600 megalitres, but there are various conflicting theories about the percentage change over the last 8000 years. Find how much water the lake had 8000 years ago, correct to the nearest 10 megalitres, if in the last 8000 years the volume has:

answer.worked:
The present volume is $100\%+60\%=160\%$ of the original volume.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Original volume}&=7600\div1.60\\\text{Original volume}&=4750\text{ ML}.\end{align*}$$
To the nearest 10 megalitres: 4750 megalitres.

The present volume is $100\%-33\%=67\%$ of the original volume.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Original volume}&=7600\div0.67\\\text{Original volume}&=\frac{760000}{67}\text{ ML}\\\text{Original volume}&\approx11340\text{ ML}.\end{align*}$$
Rounded to the nearest 10 megalitres.

The present volume is $100\%+312\%=412\%$ of the original volume.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Original volume}&=7600\div4.12\\\text{Original volume}&=\frac{190000}{103}\text{ ML}\\\text{Original volume}&\approx1840\text{ ML}.\end{align*}$$
Rounded to the nearest 10 megalitres.

The present volume is $100\%-88\%=12\%$ of the original volume.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Original volume}&=7600\div0.12\\\text{Original volume}&=\frac{190000}{3}\text{ ML}\\\text{Original volume}&\approx63330\text{ ML}.\end{align*}$$
Rounded to the nearest 10 megalitres.
